images.title: The diagonals of a square cross at right angles
images.purpose: Shows square ABCD built on a diagonal of 8 cm: equal diagonals, cut in half at O, crossing at 90°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square standing on a corner in the centre, its two diagonals crossing with a right angle mark.
images.exact_structure: One square ABCD in dark outline standing on a corner like a diamond, with A on the left, B at the top, C on the right and D at the bottom. The horizontal diagonal AC and the vertical diagonal BD are thick teal (#0072B2) lines crossing at O. A small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark sits at O. Each of the four half diagonals OA, OB, OC and OD carries one identical short amber (#E69F00) tick mark. The label 4 cm sits beside OA and the label 4 cm beside OB. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners and O sits just below and left of the crossing. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The diagonals of a square are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90°.
images.description: Shows square ABCD built on a diagonal of 8 cm: equal diagonals, cut in half at O, crossing at 90°.
images.context: AC = BD = 8 cm, OA = OB = OC = OD = 4 cm; SSS on ∆BOA and ∆BOC gives 90° at O.

image_decisions.why: The right angle at the crossing is exactly what the carpenter must add to get a square.
